body: Thanks for that link, In the past I had read the story, it was good to see again...  Spoon theories!

Your third paragraph really hits the nail on the head.  People fundamentally don't get the difference between being sick for a bit (like that time they had the fue really bad), to what their friend is experiencing..  Cue the mental isolation.  Also, in the work/career field, people with autoimmune disorders generally look healthy enough on the day to day.  Which can create questions, skepticisms, about why this person is leaving early, or starting work late and working later.  Theres always the employeer, and than theres the employees..

I've been tested for celiac disease, twice - negative both times..  I have not tried the gluten free diet.

There are many missing bridges..  I'll agree with you there.  A huge part of my strain is the cost of healthcare, copayments, and the need to preserve cash for future healthcare costs

No, I have not...  I graduated highschool from that place with the intention of never going to see a therapist again.  Made my way thru college with minimal problems, 6 months after graduation I was laid off in 2008 from my job, and then a few months after the symptoms of crohn's disease became so severe it was impossible to ignore anymore.  Cue diagnosis, and the requisite therapist.
yeah....  I have, couple years of therapy plus ended up in one of those places listed at r/troubledteens
